claude-sonnet-5.o3-mini: Hits the major plot beats (Skin Horse dialogue, becoming Real, wild-rabbit rejection, doctor's burn order, fairy transformation, final reveal) but drops the toy-cupboard hierarchy (no Timothy/model boat), the Nana tidying ritual, and the 'hurrah, seaside' beat, and compresses the transformation into vague 'something marvelous occurs' language that tells rather than shows. No music/sound cues at all, only ambient description.
claude-sonnet-5.gemini-2.5-flash: Near-complete coverage of the book including Timothy, the model boat, Nana's tidying, the seaside/'hurrah' beat, and the full illness arc; dialogue is largely verbatim. Weakest link is directibility — several scene blocks (e.g., 'WEEKS LATER') compress multiple time-jumps and actions into a single heading, and Narrator V.O. carries much of the storytelling rather than discrete filmable images. No explicit sound/music direction anywhere.
claude-sonnet-5.grok-4.5: The most complete and disciplined adaptation: full toy-hierarchy scene, all major dialogue beats verbatim, explicit 'CLOSE ON' camera directions, and a top-of-script style note ensuring visual/tonal consistency across toy and animal characters. Still no explicit sound-design or music cues, which caps the scoring dimension, but atmospheric prose (frosted silver, gaslight gold) gives a composer more to work with than most peers.
claude-sonnet-5.gpt-4o: Touches every major plot beat but in extremely thin, summarized form, losing texture (Skin Horse is 'old and wise', Nana is just 'bustling'). Several lines lean on unfilmable internal states ('listens intently, longing to become Real'; 'grateful for the love that made him Real'), and paraphrased dialogue lacks the book's lyrical specificity. No invented major content, so it remains produceable, just underdeveloped.
claude-sonnet-5.claude-sonnet-5: Otherwise the most cinematically polished script — concrete camera language ('Close on the Rabbit's button eyes'), rich atmosphere, and a strong original final beat — but it invents a named character ('Bramble') for the wild rabbit that does not exist in the source text, which per the fidelity rubric must be treated as a severe, standalone penalty on that dimension even though it doesn't break the overall story.
claude-sonnet-5.grok-4: Solid, workmanlike coverage including Timothy, the model boat, the doctor scene, and the fairy transformation, with mostly verbatim dialogue. Loses points because several scene headings cram three or four discrete actions (wheelbarrow ride + picnic + fairy hut building) into one slugline, and the illness/rejection climax is rushed without much room to breathe. No music/sound direction provided.
claude-sonnet-5.gpt-4o-mini: The condensed toy-cupboard and Skin Horse scenes retain some charm, but the complete omission of the illness/doctor/sack beat is a structural break — the audience has no idea why the Rabbit is suddenly discarded and weeping. Combined with thin, generic character description and heavy reliance on unfilmable internal-state narration, this draft needs a substantial rewrite before it could be greenlit.

JudgeSummaries.gpt-4o: Strongest: Screenplay B because it excels in adaptation fidelity and is highly directible with clear, concise action lines. Weakest: Screenplay F because it occasionally deviates from key narrative beats and has inconsistent character descriptions affecting visual continuity.
JudgeSummaries.gpt-4o-mini: Strongest: Screenplay B because it excels in adaptation fidelity and pacing, providing a strong visual narrative. Weakest: Screenplay F because it lacks the depth and engagement found in higher-rated candidates.
JudgeSummaries.o3-mini: Strongest: Screenplay E because it delivers a beautifully concise, visually direct, and cinematically rich adaptation ideal for short clips; Weakest: Screenplay D because its dense narrative detail and extended beat descriptions risk overloading the limited clip format.
JudgeSummaries.grok-4.5: Strongest: Screenplay G because it delivers near-perfect fidelity, locked visual character continuity, and densely clip-ready action lines that fully honor the 5-10s AI video constraint while preserving every emotional beat. Weakest: Screenplay B because it catastrophically abridges the source into a skeletal outline lacking essential plot pillars, character detail, and any usable directorial specificity.
JudgeSummaries.grok-4: Strongest: Screenplay E because it delivers the highest fidelity, clearest visual action lines, and consistent character anchors optimized for short AI clips. Weakest: Screenplay B because it drops essential narrative beats and provides generic descriptions that break both adaptation accuracy and directibility.
JudgeSummaries.claude-sonnet-5: Strongest: Screenplay C, because it combines the fullest, most faithful beat-for-beat coverage of the source with concrete camera-ready direction (CLOSE ON cues) and the most consistent character descriptions across scenes. Weakest: Screenplay G, because it entirely drops the illness/doctor/burning sequence that motivates the Rabbit's abandonment and tear-shedding, breaking the story's causal chain and leaving the emotional climax unearned.
JudgeSummaries.gemini-2.5-flash: Strongest: Screenplay G because it demonstrates exceptional fidelity to the source material, highly detailed and consistent character descriptions, and perfectly paced, directible beats for short video clips. Weakest: Screenplay D because it frequently relies on internal monologues or mood descriptions that are difficult to translate into concrete visual actions for AI video generation, and its fidelity is slightly less precise.
